analysis:
Examined both CI excerpts and the complete changed-range map. The visible HEAD adds .git restoration before checkout, connectivity checks, push-only cache saves, credential-free checkouts, sparse exclusions, and save-caches inputs to provider builds (.github/workflows/ci.yml:17–26, 61–94, 227–267, 467–510). PR runs cannot save these caches through the visible save steps; pinned actions and read-only contents permission remain. git fsck checks object connectivity, not authenticity of Git configuration/hooks, so security depends on who can publish and restore matching caches. No supplied evidence establishes an attacker-controlled cache writer or a concrete poisoning regression.

Sparse checkout excludes evidence archives and landing media, while Docs Lint retains its full checkout and historical-source checks (188–206). Visible release/signing/attestation checks and native admission, media, prefix, lifecycle, and cancellation-related test gates remain present. Audio fixture cache saves now require SAVE_CACHES (401–427). These workflow edits do not directly change consumer plaintext handling, cacheSalt isolation or SSD crypto (A-001/T-041), serving authorization (T-052–T-054), privileged helper authority, or billing.

Integration must reconcile the remaining changed CI sections with BASE cluster gating/caching at 703–777 and 861–893, and examine the changed provider-ci-build/cache implementations receiving save-caches at HEAD 267/510. Confirm their restore scope, source/flag identity validation, and write gating preserve artifact/test integrity (A-011/A-017/T-054). Those implementations and later HEAD changes are outside these excerpts; this local review does not establish their safety or a regression.
